Ui.Script: -- Ref Cooldown.lua's CooldownFrame_SetTimer, re-expressed: show-and-arm only when all three -- are positive, else hide. -- -- THE ONE FORK, and why it is two faithful branches rather than a guard. The reference's -- body arms a Model (`this.start = start … this:SetSequence(0)`); ours arms our native -- <Cooldown> widget, which is where 0263 put that machine. Both kinds really do reach this -- function: our own windows pass a <Cooldown>, and an addon inheriting the template below -- passes a <Model>, because an XML instance is created from ITS OWN tag and every real -- caller writes the reference's `<Model … inherits="CooldownFrameTemplate"/>`. -- -- Calling SetCooldown unconditionally is what shipped, and it raised on exactly that case: -- a Bagnon slot holding an item with a live cooldown died on -- `attempt to call method 'SetCooldown' (a nil value)` — and, because !OmniCC wraps this -- very function, it took OmniCC's countdown down with it. A Model has no sweep for this -- engine to arm (`SetSequence`/`AdvanceTime` are not bindings here), so that branch shows -- and hides the frame and nothing more: the addon's own cooldown child stays inert, which -- is a missing visual, not a broken window. function CooldownFrame_SetTimer(this, start, duration, enable) if ( start > 0 and duration > 0 and enable > 0 ) then if ( this.SetCooldown ) then this:SetCooldown(start, duration) end this:Show() else this:Hide() end end
